key_insight: MMControl extends Diffusion Transformer–based joint audio–video generation with unified multi-modal controllability, allowing users to condition both audio and video for better cross-modal alignment and more precise outputs.
problem_solved: Existing controllable generation frameworks focus on video-only control, limiting user expressiveness and producing suboptimal synchronization and alignment between generated audio and video.
method: Introduce multi-modal control tokens/conditioning into a joint Diffusion Transformer (DiT) to accept diverse controls (e.g., poses, masks, audio snippets, text) for both audio and video.
Add cross-modal alignment modules and loss terms to force coherent attention between audio and visual streams during joint diffusion sampling.
Train with multi-task supervision and modular adapters so controls can be combined flexibly at inference for fine-grained, synchronized generation.
impact: Enables practitioners to steer both sound and imagery simultaneously, improving realism and synchronization in generated clips and unlocking richer creative and production workflows for multimedia synthesis.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram of the joint DiT showing audio and video branches, multi-modal control inputs, and cross-modal alignment modules
Control palette: icons/grid showing example control types (pose, semantic mask, audio clip, text prompt) mapped to inputs
Sync visualization: timeline with waveform aligned to video frames demonstrating improved alignment before vs after MMControl
Qualitative results grid: side-by-side examples of conditional generations (different control combinations) and a small ablation chart for alignment metrics
paper_title: MMControl: Unified Multi-Modal Control for Joint Audio-Video Generation
paper_authors: Liyang Li, Wen Wang, Canyu Zhao, Tianjian Feng, Zhiyue Zhao
